text: Studies investigating resistance training under conditions of hypoxia provide further evidence of an association between metabolic stress and muscle growth. Kon and colleagues (133) found that breathing 13% oxygen during a multiset, low-load (~50% of 1RM) protocol with fairly short interset rest intervals (~1 minute) significantly heightened blood lactate levels compared to the same routine performed under normoxic conditions, providing proof of principle that hypoxia heightens metabolite accumulation. Several studies show that hypoxia enhances the hypertrophic response to resistance training.
